children.topic: Symptomatic Cholelithiasis
Primary Mechanism: Transient cystic duct obstruction
Key Diagnostic Feature(s): RUQ pain < 4–6 hrs, fatty food trigger, normal WBC/LFTs
Management: Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy
Acute Cholecystitis
Primary Mechanism: Persistent cystic duct obstruction
Key Diagnostic Feature(s): Unremitting RUQ pain > 6 hrs, Fever, leukocytosis, Murphy's sign
Management: Prompt (within 48–72 hrs) lap chole
Emphysematous Cholecystitis
Primary Mechanism: Gas-forming bacterial infection
Key Diagnostic Feature(s): Gas in gallbladder wall on imaging, elderly diabetic males
Management: Immediate cholecystectomy (Emergency!)
Gallstone Ileus
Primary Mechanism: Cholecystoduodenal fistula
Key Diagnostic Feature(s): Rigler’s triad, mechanical SBO, stone at terminal ileum
Management: Enterotomy & stone removal (leave G.B. alone!)
Ascending Cholangitis
Primary Mechanism: CBD obstruction with infection
Key Diagnostic Feature(s): Charcot’s triad / Reynold's pentad, septic shock
Management: ICU, IV fluids, IV antibiotics, emergent ERCP
